title: OMT protocol problem-code registry (v1)
description: Registry of stable machine-readable problem codes (R5). The registry map is deliberately extensible (additionalProperties with a propertyNames pattern) so later units can subdivide coarse codes additively; clients must treat an unknown code by falling back to its nearest registered coarse ancestor. message text is diagnostic only and never part of assertions.

ProblemDescriptor.description: One registry entry: what the code means, its details shape, and coarse fallback for unknown subdivided codes.

detailsShape.description: Prose description of the Problem.details fields for this code.

coarseFallback.description: Nearest coarse ancestor to interpret when this exact code is unknown to an older client; absent when the code is itself coarse.

stability.description: stable: the code will never change meaning. provisional: introduced as a subdivision and may still be folded back.

ProblemRegistry.description: Map of ProblemCode → descriptor. Open map: any key matching ^[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]+$ may appear.

SeedProblemCodes.description: The v1 seed set of coarse codes, carried forward from the TypeScript core's OmtError taxonomy. U2's pre-freeze pass subdivides these additively (e.g. ARCHIVED_READONLY under CONFLICT, DUPLICATE_MEMBER under INVALID_INPUT); the runtime plane (U5) adds its connection-identity coarse codes UNAUTHORIZED / FORBIDDEN, lifecycle code BOOTSTRAP_TIMEOUT, and the U5b resource-bound codes RATE_LIMITED / QUOTA_EXCEEDED.

SeedProblemRegistry.description: Seeded descriptors for the seven coarse codes.

CONFLICT.description: Optimistic-concurrency or state-machine conflict: revision mismatch, illegal transition, mutating a read-only archived node (the archived case is subdivided as ARCHIVED_READONLY).

INVALID_HIERARCHY.description: Hierarchy rule violation: illegal parent/child type pair (details.rule=child-type with parentType/childType), root creation of a non-epic (root-requires-epic), self-parent or descendant cycle (self-parent / descendant-cycle), cross-home move.

INVALID_INPUT.description: Payload failed semantic validation beyond schema shape: empty changeset, unsupported concurrency (subdivided as INVALID_CONCURRENCY), duplicate run member (subdivided as DUPLICATE_MEMBER), non-executable member type.

NOT_FOUND.description: Referenced home, node, run, item, or cursor does not exist. details.kind names the referent ('node' | 'run' | 'run-item') and details.id / runId+nodeId identify it.

IO.description: Filesystem or database failure while applying an operation.

UNSUPPORTED_PROTOCOL.description: Handshake or request used a protocol MAJOR the peer does not support.

SCHEMA_TOO_NEW.description: On-disk home schema is newer than this daemon understands; fail closed before any write.

UNAUTHORIZED.description: No valid credential on a request that requires one, or an expired/unknown token (details.reason in missing-credential | unknown-credential | expired-credential). Credentials are server-minted at handshake; nothing client-supplied can mint or widen one.

FORBIDDEN.description: Authenticated principal lacks the parity class, operation scope, home scope, or administrator grant for this action (details.reason in parity-adapter-only | admin-required | home-not-scoped | operation-not-granted | cross-uid-connection).

BOOTSTRAP_TIMEOUT.description: Daemon election gave up: no live daemon appeared within the loser descriptor-poll budget and the bootstrap lock could not be won (HOME_LOCKED-style coarse refusal; details.runtimeDir).

RATE_LIMITED.description: Transient capacity bound tripped (U5b/R21): too many concurrent connections or a per-home queue at depth. The request was never started; retrying after backoff can succeed (details.reason in concurrent-connections | home-queue-depth, with limit/observed where applicable).

QUOTA_EXCEEDED.description: Durable-resource quota exhausted (U5b/R21): e.g. opened-homes count or the idempotent-operation registry at its retention cap. The bound protects the host; details names rule + limit (details.rule in open-homes | idempotency-table).

SubdividedProblemRegistry.description: Subdivided codes introduced by U2's pre-freeze pass (additive; each carries a coarseFallback so older clients interpret unknown codes). Open map: any key matching ^[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]+$ may appear.

U2SubdivisionDescriptors.description: The subdivision entries frozen with the behavioral corpus (U2, incl. the U2b owner-lock codes for R2 cross-language home ownership). Each property pins the exact descriptor instance registered for that code.

summary.const: The referenced node is archived and read-only; restore it before mutating.
A run member list repeats a node id.

detailsShape.const: { nodeId: string } — the first duplicated id.

summary.const: Run concurrency must be a positive integer (v1 advertises runConcurrency: 1).

detailsShape.const: { value: number | string } — the rejected value.

HOME_LOCKED.description: Owner-lock refusal (U2b/R2): one writer per opened home; lock file <home>/home.lock (e.g. ~/.omt/home.lock), JSON body {schemaVersion, ownerKind, pid, hostname?, acquiredAt, heartbeatAt, token}. Stale holders (>30 s silent) are stolen; unknown/future schemaVersion fails closed and is never stolen. Documented residual: the marker-check-to-write window stays TOCTOU-racy until the daemon adds a kernel flock on the same path (plan U5).

summary.const: Another live writer already owns this home (per-home owner lock); only one writer may hold a home.

detailsShape.const: { pid: number | null, acquiredAt: string | null, schemaVersion?: number } — holder identity recorded in the owner lock; pid/acquiredAt are null when the lock body carries no readable identity; schemaVersion appears on incompatible-format refusals.

DAEMON_OWNS_HOME.description: Daemon-marker refusal (U2b/R2/F5): ownerKind "daemon" in <home>/home.lock always refuses TypeScript writers — even when stale — and blocks second-daemon takeover while present. Stable because takeover tooling (U6) and the daemon (U5) branch on it across languages.

summary.const: The home carries a daemon owner marker (ownerKind 'daemon'); TypeScript writers always refuse, and no second daemon may take over while it is held.

detailsShape.const: { owner: object } — the full parsed owner-lock body (schemaVersion, ownerKind, pid, hostname?, acquiredAt, heartbeatAt, token).

U4SubdivisionDescriptors.description: Subdivided codes introduced by U4's storage plane (additive; each carries a coarseFallback so older clients interpret unknown codes). Open map: any key matching ^[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]+$ may appear.

REINDEX_REQUIRED.description: Manual drift / ambiguous crash residue gate (U4/R19): observed on-disk content diverges from what the journaled plan wrote; nothing is overwritten — reindex first, then retry. Emitted by the recovery layer when a pending plan's target files were hand-edited while the writer was down, or when move source/target presence is ambiguous.

summary.const: Observed on-disk content diverges from what the journaled plan wrote (manual drift or ambiguous crash residue); nothing was overwritten — run reindex and retry.

detailsShape.const: { requiresReindex: true, commandId?: string, from?: string, to?: string } — commandId identifies the pending journal plan; from/to appear for move-drift refusals.

U5SubdivisionDescriptors.description: Runtime-plane codes introduced by U5/U5b (additive). Open map: any key matching ^[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]+$ may appear.

CANCELED.description: Client cancellation honored at a linearization-safe point (U5b): before db_committed the op aborts leaving its journal row pending-recovery (the next recovery rolls it forward); after db_committed the op completes and the cancel is ignored. details.rule=client-canceled, details.commandId, details.at names the safe point.

summary.const: The operation was canceled by the client before it could commit; any journaled residue rolls forward deterministically on the next recovery.
